newsitem.title: SPAIN: Market confidence back after Spain budget gap - Rato.
newsitem.headline: Market confidence back after Spain budget gap - Rato.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato told Congress on Tuesday that financial market confidence had returned after being shaken by news the government had discovered a 721 billion peseta gap in the 1995 budget.
"This news (of the gap) prompted a loss of credibility in the process of budgetary adjustment in Spain," Rato said.

He noted the yield spread between Spanish bonds and their German counterparts, which had widened by 10 to 20 basis points reflecting the budgetary concerns, had returned to levels seen before the gap was announced in late July.
"At this time the spread is at the same level as it was on July 26 and, therefore, it seems the market's loss of confidence has disappeared," Rato said.
He said recent budget deficit data had helped soothe market fears.
Rato said the budget gap means the former Socialist government had failed to complete its convergence programme for 1995.
"The public deficit should have been 5.9 percent but it turned out to be 6.6 percent, almost the same as in 1994," Rato said.
